Zbryzh Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews most likely settled in Zbryzh in the second half of the 18th century, reaching a population of around 750 by 1765 and drawing members from nine neighboring villages into its local community. In the 19th century, Yehoshua Burshtein served as rabbi, and a synagogue operated from 1887; by 1897, the Jewish population had declined to 281 people (17.8 percent). No information is available about what became of the community afterward. This cemetery presumably appeared on maps from the 1880s, though little visible trace remains today.
